traces.question: Panels F8a, F8b, and F8c show fracture surfaces from three points along the excess-ZrSi2 sintering-aid series described in the synthesis. Based on these panels, how does the size of the in-situ SiC grains change across the three surfaces?
traces.answer_key: The SiC grains are submicron-sized on the fracture surface with 0 vol% excess ZrSi2 (panel F8a), but appear nano-sized on the surfaces with 10 vol% and 15 vol% excess ZrSi2 (panels F8b and F8c) (o9). This shows that adding excess ZrSi2 refines the in-situ SiC from submicron to nano-sized grains (s5). Downstream, hardness, flexural strength and toughness rise then fall with ZrSi2 content, peaking at 20 vol% excess ZrSi2 (17.1 GPa, 655 MPa, 6.08 MPa m^1/2) (p2), and the paper concludes that reactive hot pressing with about 20 vol% excess ZrSi2 gives interlocking ZrB2 platelets plus nano SiC and the best mechanical properties, with the platelets dominating the toughening (c1).
traces.grading: Answer key: the numbers and labels on the evidence node o9, judge-confirmed against the panel captions, with s5, p2, c1 as the downstream chain the judge checks for consistency.

linear.text: Observation: Indentation crack path shows deflection, bridging, grain pull-out and branching into a SiC-rich region  [panels F8f]
Mechanism that produces it: Interlocked ZrB2 platelets and nano SiC trigger pull-out, crack bridging, deflection and branching, lengthening the crac  [premise: k5]
What it explains: Hardness, flexural strength and toughness rise then fall with ZrSi2, peaking at RZSZ-20 (17.1 GPa, 655 MPa, 6.08 MPa m1/

traces.question: Given the context above and the observation shown in panel F8f, what mechanism produces what is seen in that panel, and how does it account for the way hardness, flexural strength and toughness vary with ZrSi2 content across the series?
traces.answer_key: Interlocked ZrB2 platelets together with nano-scale SiC cause grain pull-out, bridging, deflection and branching of the indentation crack, extending its travel through the material (m2). This builds on the known precedent that thermal-expansion mismatch between ZrB2 and SiC leaves tangential tensile stress around SiC, which deflects cracks into SiC-rich regions (k5), and follows from the hypothesis that in-situ reaction of ZrSi2, B4C and C with excess ZrSi2 as sintering aid should give a dense, self-toughened ZrB2-SiC (h2). This toughening mechanism explains why hardness, flexural strength and toughness rise then fall with ZrSi2 content, peaking at composition RZSZ-20 with values 17.1 GPa, 655 MPa and 6.08 MPa m1/2 (p2). Overall, reactive hot pressing with about 20 vol% excess ZrSi2 yields interlocking ZrB2 platelets plus nano SiC and the best mechanical properties, with the platelets dominating the toughening (c1). The graph names a rival mechanism (node m3) against which a judge compares this account, but m3's content is not included among the node labels provided in this packet.
traces.grading: Certified judge against the graph's mechanism nodes m2 (with premises k5 and h2) and its predicted downstream effects p2 and c1, with the rival mechanism node m3 named for the comparison.
